Verified against the spec text directly (I re-read the MirrorRecv*/MirrorSend* region at the pin): (1) flow is state — TlaState carries flow, Session carries Flow ✓; recv* flow assignments match the spec exactly (register/explore/genTraces→traces, exploreSession→session, validate→validate). (2) MirrorRecvRegisterTraces fast path idle→ready+SPEC_VALIDATED is its own TlaStep ctor (no validating); Core.step folds it with MirrorSendInitialState and step_refines_tla decomposes into exactly those spec actions ✓. (3) MirrorSendSpecValidatedValid branch-on-flow encoded as two ctors (traces→ready, validate→done) ✓. (4) recvReportOk queues STEP_OK only; NEXT_STEP via separate sendNextStep ctor — Core.step's [stepOk, nextStep] refines to recvReportOk ++ [sendNextStep] (queue-empty side conditions are client-interaction obligations, documented at the ctor) ✓. (5) Ok/AllDone/Mismatch are three distinct ctors ✓. (6) ADDED: specPhases/Ms, tlaStep_preserves_phaseOk + tlaSteps_phaseOk + step_phaseOk (PhaseOk), and ClientNeverStuck mirror obligations: emit_step_responses_from_stepping, emit_initialState_target_stepping (p=idle ∧ p'=stepping), emit_explorerReady_target_exploring. (7) ext* async-job steps clearly separated with doc comments ✓. Two deliberate abstractions, both documented in-module (no Core.step behavior unmappable, so no STOP needed): (a) added TlaStep ctor sendSpecValidatedInvalid so the relation covers the spec's validate-only invalid outcome, but Core.step's oracle uses sendRegisterError for the failing validate branch — the spec equally allows RegisterError for REGISTER_VALIDATE; (b) valid/invalid collapse at tag level (spec itself abstracts the SpecInvalid payload). t15 (Phase 6 TCP + mTLS transports) completed and lake test fully green with the new transport_spec gate. Shim design: tls_shim.c is connect/accept/read/write + fingerprints/expiry only; OpenSSL policy surface explicit (TLS1.3-only, client certs required, CA chain + SAN validation, key perms 0600); SSL_CTX and SSL are Lean external objects freed by GC finalizers — the only finalizer backstop (9.7). API parity with Haskell: serveTlsOn, connectTlsPinned, certFingerprintSHA256, warnIfNearExpiry; TCP side one session per connection, drops logged and survived. Test coverage includes negatives: wrong pinned fingerprint, untrusted client cert, TLS1.2-only peer, certificate-less client, no-SAN server cert, group-readable key, near-expiry arithmetic, plus fingerprint parity against the openssl CLI. Two FFI ABI gotchas worth noting for reviewers: C-constructed Option wrappers are not ABI-safe (replaced with NULL-data external sentinels + isNull checks), and ByteArray out-params must arrive as lean_object* and use lean_sarray_cptr. Ready for review; OpenSSL config surface is the flagged #1 review target per 9.1.
